abstract: A key challenge in satellite image restoration is the presence of clouds, which introduce severe data gaps and degrade the quality of optical imagery. To address this, we propose conditioning image restoration models on stable, multimodal geospatial embeddings that capture persistent land surface characteristics. Specifically, we leverage embeddings from the AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) autoencoder, trained on fused remote sensing data over a full year. These 64-dimensional, 10 m resolution embeddings are semantically rich and robust to temporary observational gaps such as cloud cover. By augmenting multi-image restoration pipelines with AEF embeddings concatenated to input sequences, we provide strong contextual priors. Using a modified S2NAIP dataset of cloud-filtered Sentinel-2 triplets and corresponding annual AEF embeddings, a generative restoration model conditioned on these priors effectively performs cloud removal. The embeddings stabilise reconstruction under cloudy conditions by supplying missing geophysical context, unifying cloud removal with image inpainting. We compare our approach against state-of-the-art cloud removal models PMAA and CTGAN, also enhanced with AEF priors. Experimental results show that AEF embeddings consistently improve performance across both dedicated and unified architectures, highlighting the value of dense geospatial priors from foundational models for downstream remote sensing restoration tasks.
